memory_update.text: The node is not primarily about weapons demand; it is about funding velocity and cash conversion below the prime-contractor layer. Later layers should explicitly test receivables, inventory, customer advances, and funded versus unfunded backlog.

DCO, ATRO, GHM, and AADX are plausible US-listed lower-tier supplier candidates for the appropriations-pass-through and working-capital chokepoint. GHM has the clearest direct evidence of customer-funded defense capacity support.
Customer-funded grants, progress payments, and mandated pass-through clauses may be stronger signals than headline defense budget increases because they directly reduce supplier financing friction.
Do not let mega-cap primes dominate this node. Use Lockheed, RTX, Boeing, Northrop, General Dynamics, and GE Aerospace mainly as customer or funding-flow anchors, not as the main discovery universe.

node: Appropriations pass-through to lower-tier defense suppliers and working-capital bottlenecks
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-stock universe around a financial-plumbing chokepoint in the defense industrial base: lower-tier suppliers may have demand and backlog, but production can be constrained by slow appropriations flow, uneven prime purchase orders, high receivables/inventory needs, customer-funded capacity projects, or debt-heavy balance sheets. The underfollowed discovery lane is more relevant than mega-cap primes here. Candidate emphasis is on US-listed aerospace/defense component, subsystem, and mission-critical manufacturing suppliers with defense backlog or capacity expansion needs that could be helped if Congress or DoD forces appropriated funds, progress payments, supplier financing, or customer grants farther down the supply chain. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
